answer: Dynamic Storage Rent Decay. Each active node must continuously deposit assets into a cryptographic vault to maintain protocol indexing rights. This rental rate scales exponentially with the global density of connected peers within a local network ledge, forcing attackers to fund capital for every synthetic node. As the sybil cluster expands, the per-identity storage fee outpaces any mining yield it can extract. Consequently, an adversary attempting to saturate the routing graph faces immediate financial exhaustion, forcing rogue agents to wander off and abandon their unviable swarm.
